text: Fill in the blanks: __________ occur(s) when two or more threads are blocked forever but both appear active. __________ occur(s) when two or more threads try to complete a related task at the same time.

answers.text: Livelock, Deadlock
Deadlock, Starvation
Race conditions, Deadlock
Livelock, Race conditions
Starvation, Race conditions
Deadlock, Livelock

correct.description: Livelock occurs when two or more threads are conceptually blocked forever, although they are each still active and trying to complete their task[cite: 181]. A race condition is an undesirable result that occurs when two tasks are completed at the same time, which should have been completed sequentially[cite: 182]. For these reasons, D is the only correct answer[cite: 183].

text: Which happens when more tasks are submitted to a thread executor than available threads?

answers.text: The thread executor will throw an exception when a task is submitted that is over its thread limit.
The task will be added to an internal queue and completed when there is an available thread.
The thread executor will discard any task over its thread limit.
The call to submit the task to the thread executor will wait until there is a thread available before continuing.
The thread executor creates new temporary threads to complete the additional tasks.

correct.description: If a task is submitted to a thread executor, and the thread executor does not have any available threads, the call to the task will return immediately with the task being queued internally by the thread executor[cite: 184]. For this reason, B is the only correct answer[cite: 184].

text: Which of the following properties of concurrency are true? (Choose all that apply.)

answers.text: By itself, concurrency does not guarantee which task will be completed first.
Concurrency always improves the performance of an application.
Computers with a single processor do not benefit from concurrency.
Applications with many resource-heavy tasks tend to benefit more from concurrency than ones with CPU-intensive tasks.
Concurrent tasks do not share the same memory.

correct.description: By itself, concurrency does not guarantee which task will be completed first, so A is correct[cite: 244]. Furthermore, applications with numerous resource requests will often be stuck waiting for a resource, which allows other tasks to run[cite: 245]. Therefore, they tend to benefit more from concurrency than CPU-intensive tasks, so D is also correct[cite: 246]. B is incorrect because concurrency may in fact make an application slower if it is truly single-threaded in nature[cite: 247, 248]. C is incorrect because single-processor CPUs have been benefiting from concurrency for decades[cite: 249]. Finally, E is incorrect; there are numerous examples in this chapter of concurrent tasks sharing memory[cite: 250].
